label: <DEL> step of long (L=8-9) sequences starting with a and/or with u as 2nd token
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.007% of steps). About 99% of its activation mass is at the delimiter step, and almost all of that is in L=8 (28%) or L=9 (70%) sequences. It essentially never fires in the copy phase, apart from 3 weak original-phase activations at the last original token. Activation depends on what the sequence started with. Sequences whose first token is a hold about 62% of the mass (15x lift), and sequences whose second token is u hold about 51%. Every top activation starts with a u, and having both together gives the largest values. A few other tokens appearing anywhere in the sequence (o, x, r, 3, g) go with stronger activation, and s, 0 and 1 go with weaker activation. The predicate covers about 83% of the mass, but precision is only about 3%: most long a-initial or ?u-initial sequences do not activate it. Even a-u-initial sequences fire only about 36% of the time. So the feature reads a graded hidden-state direction that mixes many tokens and that no simple predicate captures. It does not fire on short sequences (L<=6), on copy steps, or on ordinary original-token inputs.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig2=u (+4.09), orig1=u (+2.44), orig0=a (+2.30), phase=1 & out_tok=a (+2.18), orig5=o (+2.12), phase=1 & out_tok=u (+2.12). Lower it: in_first=0 (-4.61), orig7=- (-3.75), in_count=1 (-1.97), next_out=- (-1.86).
